da-non-sequitur.evidence: (S↔P column of thm:topological-mass row) Ref resolves to library `QOU.Torsion.mass_decomposition_categorical` (lean/QOU/Torsion/mass_decomposition_categorical.lean:51). Its context class carries `mass_decomposes : Prop`, `decomposition_active : mass_decomposes` and `impl_… : mass_decomposes → mass = Σ_{n<N} mass_level n`, so it is self-assuming with a free-Prop carrier. It also states a different decomposition (a sum over tower levels) from the theorem's ‖tr_desc‖ + Σᵢ‖tr_trans(ϱ,pᵢ)‖. The sibling `.lean` proves only the triangle inequality, and equality under non-negativity hypotheses. prf:topological-mass says itself that it gives only an upper bound, and that equality is "open". prf:topological-mass-categorical cites lem:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace as an additive split ‖tr τα‖ + ‖tr(α−τα)‖, but that lemma states the Pythagorean m² = a² + b² and stresses "not additively". So the proof contradicts the lemma it cites. Its transient step uses the false "disjoint supports ⇒ norm of sum = sum of norms". The statement also says the orthogonal splitting makes the mass "decompose additively", which is the same error (Pythagoras gives √(a²+b²))

[full review 2026-11-21; proof rewritten to the upper bound] The proof now concludes only m(rho) <= norm Hol + sum norm MI over E_i, and says equality is open; that matches prop:topological-mass-upper-bound, and the chain of inequalities follows from the three cited lemmas. Three gaps. (1) Step 1 uses the eigenspace lemma, which now takes the multiplicative-integral factorisation as a hypothesis; this proof never states or discharges it. (2) The last line writes sum Phi_q(z_i) without the norm that appears in every earlier line. (3) The title 'Proof of Topological Decomposition of Mass' and uses[] still present it as a proof of the decomposition; it proves the archimedean bound, and its uses[] omits the eigenspace, holonomy and transient lemmas it actually cites.

Re-read at 50d405d. prf:topological-mass, one of the two proofs of prop:topological-mass-upper-bound, now uses conj:topological-mass-dilogarithm (was lem:). The closing sentence 'Each exceptional-divisor summand equals the quantum dilogarithm Phi_q(z_i) by (quantum dilogarithm evaluation), so the bound reads m(rho) <= ... + sum Phi_q(z_i). □' cites a conjecture as an established step inside a proof. The proposition's own statement has no Phi_q, so the proved inequality is unaffected, and the conjectural-propagation audit does not flag it (proof-block uses are not counted). The sentence should be conditional ('if the conjecture holds').
